turn_text: Now, I believe the Postmaster, during the previous administration, there was a new Postmaster named, it must have been about a year or two ago, a couple of years ago, who did kind of start some of these reforms. I'm sure you're familiar with that situation. How much does that have to do with these reforms?

Well, it's a great question. There was a lot of concern in 2020 at the way that the Postmaster General was cutting back service and shutting down distribution centers. There was a great concern about what impact that was going to have on people, especially right as we were looking at folks using the post office to mail in their absentee ballots. This is a piece of legislation that will make sure that those kinds of service cuts don't happen in the future. And it also addresses the underlying financial challenge that was leading to some of those efforts to cut service. There's something that most people don't know, which is that quite a few years ago, the post office was required to kind of pre-pay its pension expense 75 years into the future. Now no other federal government agency or private sector business pre-pays that kind of responsibility into the future. And so what we did with this bill is we got rid of that which will save a lot of money and also make it so that the post office is on a secure financial footing.
